item.text: I’m taking another pass through the current file to look for the next maintainability win that doesn’t change behavior. Given the repository is still a single Java file, I’ll bias toward a clean API and a better separation between library code and runnable demo.

I’ve identified a worthwhile cleanup: validate heap arguments centrally and move the runnable example out of the utility class. That keeps the core API focused, makes misuse fail fast, and leaves the heap implementation easier to reuse.

I caught an edge case while wiring the new overload: empty arrays should remain a no-op instead of tripping validation. I’m adjusting that before compiling so the public API stays predictable on degenerate inputs.
The API cleanup is done. I’m compiling both classes and running the demo to ensure the refactor didn’t change the heap result or introduce argument-validation regressions.
Compilation succeeded. I’m running the new demo entrypoint now, since the old `main` moved out of the utility class, and I want to confirm the public-facing behavior is still intact.

I did another cleanup pass and separated the reusable heap logic from the demo.
